expectations.evidence: commerce/gift_card/ — explicitly reasoned per §3.1: 'El subcontexto se nombra en snake_case coincidiendo con el agregado'

Every file uses `from x import y` then `y.Z` (e.g. `from commons.domain import aggregates, money` then `aggregates.AggregateRoot`); aliases used correctly for collisions (`base_value_objects`, `commons_exceptions`)
`balance: money.NonNegativeMoney`, redemption amount typed `money.PositiveMoney`; even added a missing `__sub__` to the shared `Money` class rather than hand-rolling subtraction
`expires_at: base_value_objects.PosixTime`, uses `PosixTime.now()`/`.from_datetime()`, never raw datetime in the domain; ORM stores `expires_at: Mapped[int]` as BigInteger microseconds
`_publish_events(uow, gift_card)` called inside `with uow.transaction():` in both `issue_gift_card` and `redeem_gift_card`
Explicitly walked the decision tree ('¿el caso de uso muta exactamente una instancia de agregado? → Sí... §10.1') and named the Middle Man smell as the reason not to add one
`GiftCardNotActiveError`, `GiftCardExpiredError`, `InsufficientGiftCardBalanceError`, `GiftCardNotFoundError` — one per invalid transition, all subclassing `commons.domain.exceptions`

suggestions.reason: The run surfaced a real gap in the skill's own Money reference (missing __sub__) and fixed it in-place rather than hand-rolling subtraction elsewhere — worth backporting __sub__ into the actual references/domain-and-application.md and ARCHITECTURE.md so future runs don't have to rediscover this.

eval_feedback.overall: All 10 assertions pass with genuine, well-reasoned evidence (not superficial) — the decision-tree walk-through for 'no orchestrator' and the correction of an incomplete Money reference show real understanding, not pattern-matching against the golden path example.
